quiz.title: Solving Equations
quiz.source_reference: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(a)–(l). Questions: Source Files/2iec/Pure Chapt 01 Quadratics/C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8. Worked answers: Source Files/2iec/Pure Chapt 01 Quadratics/C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Answers - Worksheet E, page 3). © Solomon Press.
quiz.instructions: Solve each equation over the real numbers. Choose the option containing every real solution. Exclude any value that makes a denominator in the original equation zero.

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(a)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq0\). Multiply the equation by \(x\):

\[x^2-5x+4=0.\]

Factorise: \((x-1)(x-4)=0\).

Therefore \(x=1\) or \(x=4\). Both satisfy the original equation and its denominator restriction.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(a); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(b)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq0\). Multiply by \(x\):

\[x^2-10=3x\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^2-3x-10=0.\]

Factorise: \((x+2)(x-5)=0\).

Therefore \(x=-2\) or \(x=5\). Both are valid in the original equation.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(b); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(c)
questions.working:
Take out the common factor \(x\), rather than dividing by \(x\) and losing the zero solution:

\[x(2x^2-x-3)=0.\]

Factorise the quadratic: \[x(2x-3)(x+1)=0.\]

Therefore \(x=0\), \(x=\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x=-1\). All three satisfy the original equation.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(c); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(d)
questions.working:
Expand and rearrange:

\[10x^2-x^4=9\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^4-10x^2+9=0.\]

Factorise as a quadratic in \(x^2\): \[(x^2-1)(x^2-9)=0.\]

Thus \(x^2=1\) or \(x^2=9\). Taking both positive and negative square roots gives \(x=\pm1\) or \(x=\pm3\).
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(d); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(e)
questions.working:
The original denominators require \(x\neq0\). Multiply by \(x^2\):

\[5+4x-x^2=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^2-4x-5=0.\]

Factorise: \((x+1)(x-5)=0\).

Therefore \(x=-1\) or \(x=5\). Neither is excluded by the original denominators, and both satisfy the original equation.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(e); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(f)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq4\). Multiply by \(x-4\):

\[x-6=x(x-4)=x^2-4x.\]

Rearrange and factorise: \[x^2-5x+6=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad(x-2)(x-3)=0.\]

Therefore \(x=2\) or \(x=3\). Both satisfy the original equation and neither equals \(4\).
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(f); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(g)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq-3\). Multiply by \(x+3\):

\[(x+5)(x+3)=3.\]

Expand and rearrange: \[x^2+8x+15=3\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^2+8x+12=0.\]

Factorise: \((x+6)(x+2)=0\). Therefore \(x=-6\) or \(x=-2\). Both are valid in the original equation.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(g); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(h)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq0\). Multiply by \(x^2\):

\[x^4-4=3x^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^4-3x^2-4=0.\]

Factorise: \[(x^2+1)(x^2-4)=0.\]

The equation \(x^2=-1\) has no real solutions. From \(x^2=4\), \(x=\pm2\). Both satisfy the original equation and its denominator restriction.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(h); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(i)
questions.working:
Rearrange: \[4x^4+7x^2-2=0.\]

Factorise as a quadratic in \(x^2\): \[(4x^2-1)(x^2+2)=0.\]

Thus \(x^2=\frac{1}{4}\) or \(x^2=-2\). The latter has no real solutions.

Taking both square roots of \(\frac{1}{4}\) gives \(x=\pm\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(i); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(j)
questions.working:
The original denominators require \(x\neq3\) and \(x\neq-2\). Multiply by \((3-x)(x+2)\):

\[2x(x+2)=3-x.\]

Expand and rearrange: \[2x^2+4x=3-x\quad\Rightarrow\quad2x^2+5x-3=0.\]

Factorise: \((2x-1)(x+3)=0\). Therefore \(x=\frac{1}{2}\) or \(x=-3\). Both satisfy the original equation and neither is an excluded value.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(j); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(k)
questions.working:
The original denominators require \(x\neq-3\) and \(x\neq0\). Multiply by \(x(x+3)\):

\[x(2x+1)=2(x+3).\]

Expand and rearrange: \[2x^2+x=2x+6\quad\Rightarrow\quad2x^2-x-6=0.\]

Factorise: \((2x+3)(x-2)=0\). Therefore \(x=-\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x=2\). Both satisfy the original equation and its denominator restrictions.
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(k); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).

questions.section: Worksheet E — Exercise 6: Solve each equation
questions.title: 6(l)
questions.working:
The original denominator requires \(x\neq-2\). Multiply by \(x+2\):

\[7-3x(x+2)=2(x+2).\]

Expand and rearrange: \[7-3x^2-6x=2x+4\quad\Rightarrow\quad3x^2+8x-3=0.\]

Factorise: \((3x-1)(x+3)=0\). Therefore \(x=\frac{1}{3}\) or \(x=-3\). Both satisfy the original equation and neither equals \(-2\).
questions.source_ref: C1 Algebra, Worksheet E, Exercise 6(l); C1 Algebra - Questions.pdf, PDF page 8; C1 Algebra - Answers.pdf, PDF page 13 (Worksheet E answers, page 3).
